label: October 2026

biggest.lede: We move the clock closer to midnight by one second as worsening Ebola outbreak and severe Australian storms increase immediate biological and climate risks.

title: Clock ticks closer to midnight one second
summary: The Doomsday Clock began October 2026 at 85 seconds to midnight and ended at 84 seconds, moving closer to midnight by one second. The shift was driven primarily by a worsening Ebola outbreak in the Congo and severe storms in Australia, raising biological and climate risks.

sections.heading: What moved the clock
body: The clock was moved closer to midnight by one second on 2026-10-31 because experts judged the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, now with over 5,000 deaths, and the emergence of suspected cases in Nigeria, as escalating biological danger. Additionally, severe storms across Australia heightened immediate climate risk, prompting the overall assessment of increased danger.

sections.heading: Where the experts disagreed
body: No experts disagreed on the direction of the clock this month; all votes were either hold or worse, with no day showing both a "worse" and a "better" vote.

sections.heading: What to watch next month
body: Monitor the spread of Ebola in Central Africa and any further developments in Australian weather extremes, as both could influence the clock’s position in November.
